message.content:
The bug: the `while` loop follows `default_table[j]` to parents without re-validating that `parent < d->state_count`. The check at line 6 only validates the initial `j = state`. Once we move to `parent`, `d->default_table[parent]` could be out of bounds (or `parent` itself could be out of bounds if `default_table[j]` was changed... but actually line 6 checks `default_table[state]` which is the first parent). Wait — line 6 checks `d->default_table[j]` where `j = state`, so the first parent is validated. But then `j = parent`, and the loop reads `d->is_differential[j]` and `d->default_table[j]` for the new `j` without checking `j < state_count` or `default_table[j] < state_count`.

Actually, `parent` comes from `default_table[j]` which was validated at line 6 only for the initial `j`. For subsequent iterations, `default_table[j]` is read at line 10 without validation. So the missing recheck is at line 10/11.

The primary bug is introduced where the parent is used without re-validation — line 10 reads `default_table[j]` and line 11 assigns it to `j` without bounds check. The smallest set capturing the bug is line 10 (where the unchecked read happens) — but the comment on line 11 explicitly notes "parent not rechecked here", pointing to line 11 as the bug location.

The bug is that `parent` is not validated before being used as `j`. Line 11 is where the unchecked value becomes `j`.

Answer: 11
